filename: Incorporating Multivariate Consistency in ML-Based Weather Forecasting with Latent-space Constraints.pdf
title: Incorporating Multivariate Consistency in ML-Based Weather Forecasting with Latent-space Constraints
testbed_rationale: The study uses coarsened global ERA5 reanalysis to develop a latent-space constraint loss for deterministic weather forecasting and does not produce or release a new parameterization benchmark dataset.
pain_points: Autoregressive rollout training in model space with variable-specific MSE loss ignores cross-variable error covariance and scale dependency, causing blurred forecasts and loss of physical realism at long leads.
Explicitly representing the reanalysis error covariance matrix in model space is computationally intractable due to extreme dimensionality (> 10^12).
Evaluating the loss in latent space substantially increases computational training costs due to encoder forward passes.
Key assumptions for the latent-space surrogate (reconstruction error, local linearity, and diagonal error covariance) are only approximately satisfied in practice.
Long-range deterministic RMSE of the latent-constrained model still degrades relative to model-space MSE beyond 5 days, highlighting the need for probabilistic formulations at longer lead times.
extraction_notes: The paper reframes rollout training as weak-constraint 4D-Var (WC-4DVar) and applies constraints in the latent space of a pretrained Swin-Transformer autoencoder to maintain multivariate physical consistency.
